title: Light before the sun
opening_question: If the sun was made on Day 4, what was the light on Day 1?

steps.question: What does the text say happened on Day 1?

facts.text: "Light" on Day 1 is the Hebrew 'or: "illumination or (concretely) luminary". God "called the light Day", and the first day has "the evening and the morning" before any sun is made.
The text does not say where the light of Day 1 came from. It says only that God spoke: "Let there be light: and there was light".

steps.question: What was made on Day 4, and what does the text say it is for?

facts.text: "Lights" on Day 4 is a different word, ma'or: "a luminous body or luminary". Both words come from the same root (H215). Day 1 has light itself; Day 4 has the bodies that give it.
Ma'or also stands for "the greater light" and "the lesser light". The text says what they are for: "for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years" and "to give light upon the earth".
Day 4 does not use the words sun and moon; it says "two great lights". Psalm 136 names them: "The sun to rule by day" and "The moon and stars to rule by night".

steps.question: What does John say was there in the beginning, and what does he call the light?

facts.text: John opens with the first words of Genesis: "In the beginning". "Light" here is the Greek phos: "luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative)".
John says of the Word: "In him was life; and the life was the light of men", and "the light shineth in darkness".

steps.question: Who is called "the light of the world" in these verses?
What does this verse say God is?
What gives light where there is no sun or moon?

facts.text: Isaiah and Revelation both speak of light without sun or moon: "the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light", and "the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof". Like Day 1, this light does not depend on the sun.

steps.question: More verses on light and where it comes from. Some say God forms light, some say God is light, some say He dwells in it. What does each one say?

facts.text: Paul uses Genesis 1:3 for what God does in a person: "God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts". The BSB: "Let light shine out of darkness".
James calls God "the Father of lights"; Paul says He is "dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto".

steps.question: Living it out: God who said "Let there be light" has "shined in our hearts". What does Jesus say about following Him, and what are we to do with the light?

facts.text: "if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another"; "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works".

remember.text: God said "Let there be light" on the first day; the sun and moon came on the fourth.
"God is light, and in him is no darkness at all"
Jesus said "I am the light of the world".
In the city, "the Lamb is the light thereof".
Some verses say God forms light, some that He is light, some that He dwells in it. You weigh them.
